terms.gloss: keep close behind me, follow closer
terms.grammar: imperative of subsequor; propius (comparative of prope) with the accusative mē
evidence: Plaut. Bacch. 723: Cedo manum ac subsequere propius mē ad forēs.
terms.comment: Said in Plautus by a man drawing his companion close to look in at a door: give me your hand and keep close.

terms.grammar: ā latere (+ genitive or a possessive: ā latere meō)
evidence: Cic. Lael. 1: ut, quoad possem et licēret, ā senis latere numquam discēderem
terms.comment: Cicero’s phrase for keeping close to someone all the time; to a child, Nē ā latere meō discēdās.

phrases.english: What a crowd! Stay close to me.

phrases.latin: Cedo manum ac subsequere propius mē ad forēs. intrō īnspice.
phrases.english: Give me your hand and keep close to me, up to the door. Look inside.

phrases.latin: ut, quoad possem et licēret, ā senis latere numquam discēderem
phrases.english: so that, as far as I could and was allowed, I never left the old man’s side

sources: Lewis & Short: subsequor · Lewis & Short: prope · Lewis & Short: latus
